_comment: Overlay on history/thresholds.json for a project whose project.json says "domain": "pivotal-history". Each key here REPLACES the base key of the same name; every other base key (minQuoteWords, verbatimCopyWindowWords, eraShareMax, sourceRatio, introWords, the editor) holds unchanged. Read by tools/_hw.thresholds(project). Like the base file, these are first calibrations: the pilot measures them.
_eventEvidenceRequired: On from the first scout. Every dossier event carries a verbatim quote that richness.py checks, so a scout on a cheaper model can miss an event but cannot add one (design D8).
_biographyMinLifeStages: An episode is never a biography. Its events carry a `phase` (prelude, march, siege, battle, aftermath) where a life's carry a `lifeStage`, and four phases inside one season are still one episode. 99 keeps richness.py from calling it a life; the mode is episode, or ensemble for a long campaign told through its turning points.
_encyclopediaPublishers: Summaries of other work. Tier A needs sources beyond them.
_licenceCleanClasses: richness.py counts licenceClean (independent groups holding at least one source a paid book may quote and reuse, history/sourcing.md §5) and licenceCleanWords. Facts-only sources still give facts; licence-clean ones also give scenes and quotations.
_tiers: The base tiers plus licenceClean, and one source beyond the encyclopedias at tier B: an episode told only from Wikipedia has nothing new to say. lifeStages counts an episode's phases.
_opening: voice.md §6, the author's decision of 2026-10-18: an episode opens with its GROUND (a map or plan of the place, period or drawn from a free basemap, or a photograph of the site), not a face. images.py opening sets it in the portrait's slot with the same licence, caption and placement checks; gate.py story refuses an opening whose caption does not name the place by one of the dossier's `place` names (its aliases when it has none). A life (no domain) still opens with its subject's portrait.

l1DeclarationExamples: Had you stood on the outer wall that morning, …
If you had been aboard the Monitor, …

_pov: voice.md §2, the point-of-view ladder. l1Requires: an immersive passage is earned by a participant's or eyewitness's own account (marked ownWords, with its span), as length is earned by words about the subject; richness.py dossier writes computed.pov as L0 or L0+L1. l1DeclarationPatterns: the first sentence of every L1 passage must match one, so the reader can see the mode change. l1ExemptRules: base rules that do not fire INSIDE a declared passage (stage_direction: 'in front of you stands' is the declared frame); every other rule still does, and outside a passage nothing is exempt. l1ShareMax: L1 words over chapter words. L2, historical fiction, is not a mode here.
